slides.1.title: 🎯 Level 1 Key Review
slides.1.points.0: 🍷 Italy is the world's #1 wine exporter with 350+ native varieties
slides.1.points.1: 📊 Classification: DOCG (highest) > DOC > IGT > Vino da Tavola
slides.1.points.2: 🏔️ The Apennines run through the country; three climate zones: Continental / Mediterranean / Hot Mediterranean
slides.1.points.3: 🗺️ North (Piemonte, Veneto, Lombardy): high-quality reds and sparkling wines
slides.1.points.5: 🗺️ South + Islands (Sicily, Sardinia): rich, indigenous varieties
slides.1.points.6: 👑 Nebbiolo → Barolo DOCG (the King) + Barbaresco DOCG (the Queen)
slides.1.points.7: 🌹 Sangiovese → Chianti Classico, Brunello di Montalcino
slides.1.points.8: 💪 Barbera: high acid, low tannin — excellent everyday drinking, Piemonte's workhorse
slides.1.points.9: 🌊 Veneto's three stars: Amarone (Appassimento) / Soave / Prosecco (Glera)
slides.1.points.11: 🥂 Franciacorta DOCG: traditional-method sparkling — Italy's Champagne
slides.1.points.13: 🍇 Five red varieties: Nebbiolo / Sangiovese / Barbera / Montepulciano / Nero d'Avola
slides.1.points.14: 🤍 Five white varieties: Pinot Grigio / Trebbiano / Garganega / Verdicchio / Vermentino
slides.1.points.15: 🍽️ Regional pairing principle: What grows together, goes together
slides.1.points.16: 🍕 Tomato sauce → high-acid Sangiovese; cream sauce → white wine
slides.1.points.17: 🧀 Blue cheese Gorgonzola → sweet Moscato d'Asti
slides.1.points.18: 📜 Marsala = Sicilian fortified wine; Sforzato = Valtellina dried-grape Nebbiolo
slides.1.points.19: 🎓 Congratulations on completing Level 1! Ready for Level 2?
